doc: The NEUTRAL OBSERVATION the decision server reads: one plain object per game per seat, integers and booleans only. Every `seat` group is an object keyed by its field names in the order listed; after them, `cities` is a list with one object per LIVING city of the seat, in the seat's city-ARRAY order (TS `seat.cities`: founding order, a lost city spliced out, a gained one appended), each keyed by the `city` fields in the order listed. Then `targets`, an object keyed by the `targets` fields in the order listed (the tile planes the unit planner walks toward), and `units`, a list with one object per LIVING unit of the seat in its unit-ARRAY order (TS `state.units` filtered to the seat; at most UNIT_SLOTS), each keyed by the `unit` fields in the order listed. Field kinds: bool = a flag; int = a plain integer (a table index, a tile index, a count, a price); city = one of THIS seat's living cities named by its CENTRE tile, -1 where none; list = a list of plain integers, laid out as its meaning says (a dense list indexed by a table index, or ascending indices); table = a list of fixed-width rows of plain integers, ascending (in `geo`: one row per major seat, as its meaning lays it out); matrix = a list of lists over the major seats, [a][b]; floats = a list of numbers. Every price is an exact integer: no field carries a fraction, `vec` aside. The `head` fields close the per-seat object. `geo` is ONE object per GAME, keyed by its fields in the order listed: the diplomatic table every seat's agreements and deals are decided from at once. `world` is ONE object per GAME, keyed by its fields in the order listed: the facts every seat sees alike, the one group BOTH engines emit so far (the gate compares the two every turn before the decide). `static` names the facts of a game that never change, which the server builds once from rules.json and the world's dimensions and hands the driver beside the observations. Emitters: gpu/core/neutral.py (GPU, every section); cpu/core/decideObs.ts (TS, `world`).

buy: the city holding the cheapest completable gold-buyable building
the treasury clears its price plus the peace-gold reserve
a gold settler buy is affordable and the spawn city has the pop
a gold military unit buy is open (under 2x cities, a candidate type)
a gold tile buy is open
Monumentality: a faith builder buy is open
Monumentality: a faith settler buy is open
where a bought unit spawns: the capital, else the first living city
a faith worship-building buy is open
a faith missionary buy is open
a faith apostle buy is open
a faith inquisitor buy is open
a faith warrior monk buy is open
a levy is open and the seat is at war with a major
a faith naturalist buy is open
a faith rock band buy is open
a faith class-building buy is open (Valletta)
the building's table index, -1 where none
a faith land combat unit buy is open
the unit type index, -1 where none
a faith Great Person patronage is open
a gold Great Person patronage is open
a gold district buy is open
a faith district buy is open
route: the origin city of the trade route this seat would open
its destination: a CENTRE tile, or -(2 + city-state index); -1 where none
nuke: the WMD device index a silo would launch, -1 where none
research: per tech table index: its effective research cost (`effectiveResearchCostIn`: the base cost, boosted and js-rounded — a whole number), -1 where the tech is not open (`availableTechsIn`)
per civic table index: the same for civics (`availableCivicsIn`)
policy: the policy card table indices this seat may slot now (`unlockedPolicyIds`), ascending; empty without a government
the adopted government's slots by kind (`fitPolicies`' governmentSlots, wonder extras included): [military, economic, diplomatic, wildcard]; all 0 without a government
war: the war head's width (`warTargets`): every other major in ascending seat order, then the whole city-state roster in index order; a war COLUMN below is a position in that list
the target columns this seat may declare war on now, ascending
the target columns it may sue for peace with now, ascending

per MAJOR target column (the war head's leading columns, one per other major): the war kind a declaration there takes by default (`defaultWarKind`: the cheapest casus belli held), -1 where none is held or the column is not in `declare`
per MAJOR target column: the leader's own buffed kind where it is allowed (`WAR_BUFF_ROWS`), else the default; -1 likewise
this seat is at war with anyone: a major, a city-state, the Free Cities or the barbarians
envoy: per city-state index (the roster index, fixed for the game): the envoys this seat holds there, -1 where it has not met the city-state or the city-state is gone
congress: the two resolution table indices (CONGRESS_RESOLUTIONS) on the ANNOUNCED slate of the Regular Session the coming turn would hold (TS `worldCongress`: every CONGRESS_INTERVAL turn from CONGRESS_MIN_ERA; the slate is `state.congressSlate`), -1 in a slot with no resolution or on a turn with no session
per slate slot: the outcome this seat prefers on that resolution (`preference`), -1 where the slot is -1
per slate slot: the target it prefers (`preference`), -1 where the slot is -1
that session also holds the Diplomatic Victory resolution (world era >= CONGRESS_DV_MIN_ERA)

the Diplomatic Victory leader's major seat index when `dv`: the most diplomatic victory points among majors holding a city, ties to the lower index (the scan inside TS `runDvResolution`); -1 otherwise
a Special Session would sit on the coming turn: a called emergency whose hiatus has run out, the Congress open (TS `specialSessions`)
the favor price step of one extra vote (`buyVotes`' curve)
gp: per Great Person class: the individual on offer (`gpOffer`: a roster index, -1 a draw pending, -2 exhausted); empty where the world has no Great Person classes
per class: the major seat index that passed on the standing offer (`gpPassedBy`), -1 nobody
per class: the offer's frozen price in Great Person points (a whole number)
per class: this seat's Great Person points, floored
belief: the seat may found its religion now (`canFoundReligion`): no seat ban, no religion yet, a pantheon, a completed Holy Site or Stonehenge, an activated Great Prophet
the seat may enhance its religion now (`canEnhanceReligion`): founded, not yet enhanced, a second activated Great Prophet
per religion belief class (BELIEF_CLASSES: Follower, Worship, Founder, Enhancer): the class catalog row the seat's religion holds, -1 none
the Follower catalog rows no religion holds, ascending
the Worship catalog rows no religion holds, ascending
the Founder catalog rows no religion holds, ascending
the Enhancer catalog rows no religion holds, ascending

city: the city's CENTRE tile, its name on the wire
the settlers on order in its queue, at any depth
the production columns it may queue now (the one production layout, cpu/core/prodLayout.ts), ascending; empty while its queue has no room

for every OPEN district column: each plot the district may go on, as [column, tile, adjacency] — the adjacency the district would earn there (floored; 0 for the types with no adjacency yield) — ascending by column, then tile
per district table index: the specialist slots the district offers (`citySpecialistSlots`); empty where the world has no districts
per district table index: the citizens pinned into its slots (`City.specialistPref`), -1 where the automatic rule fills it; empty likewise
every plot the city may work (`workableTiles`), as [tile, resource priority, locked]: the plot's resource priority (0 = none) and 1 where its citizen pin is set (`Tile.locked`); ascending by tile

every plot a sibling city holds that this city may claim (`swapTileOk`), as [tile, the holder's centre, worked, locked]: worked = 1 where any of the seat's cities works it, locked = 1 where its pin is set; ascending by tile
targets: the tiles a Builder has improvement work on (the TS driver's `jobTiles`: an owned tile that is pillaged, holds a pillaged district, or is bare and takes an improvement it has unlocked), ascending; empty where improvements are off or the seat holds no Builder with a charge

the tiles a Military Engineer has work on (the TS driver's `engTiles`: a road it may lay, an engineer improvement site, or a 20%-charge site), ascending; empty where improvements are off or the seat holds no Military Engineer with a charge

the CENTRE tiles of every living major city not following this seat's religion (the TS driver's `spreadTargets`), ascending; empty where the seat founded no religion or holds no Missionary or Apostle with a charge

the tiles a city may be founded on (`canFoundCity`: unowned, settleable, bare of district and wonder, at least 4 from every living city and city-state centre), ascending; empty where the seat holds no Settler or stands at the city cap
the tiles an Archaeologist may excavate (a dig underfoot on unowned or own ground) while a museum slot takes an Artifact, ascending; empty where the seat holds no Archaeologist with a charge
the tiles that ANCHOR a legal National Park rhombus (`parkClusterLegal` on any of the tile's clusters), ascending; empty where the seat holds no Naturalist with a charge

for every Great Person site a living person of this seat with a charge walks toward (its `gpSite`, `gpArg`; never site 1, which activates where it stands): each tile it may be spent on, as [site, arg, tile], ascending
the tiles holding a Tribal Village, ascending

the tiles a unit at war marches on first: an unpillaged improvement, or a complete unpillaged district, on ground owned by a seat this one is at war with (majors and city-states; Free City ground is not a march target), ascending; empty where the seat is at war with nobody

every living city of a seat this one is at war with, as [seat, centre]: the owner's seat id (a major's index, 100 + a city-state's index, 300 the Free Cities) and the city's CENTRE tile, ascending; the march takes the nearest, the seat id then the centre breaking a distance tie; empty where the seat is at war with nobody
unit: the tile the unit stands on
a Great Person's roster position within its class, -1 for every other unit
a Great Person's site code (GP_SITES: where its charge is spent), -1 for every other unit
that site's argument (the district table index for site 0), -1 where none
the unit action columns it may take now (the one unit action layout, rules.json `actions.unit`), ascending
head: turn
int
the engine turn the coming step plays (`state.turn`: 1 before the first step); the driver's draws key on turn - 1
vec
floats
the seat's RL observation vector (`observeSeat`, cpu/core/observe.ts), the one field that is not integral: compared to a tolerance, and read by the driver through `ladder.split`
geo: per major seat: 1 while the seat is alive
per major seat: its living cities
per major seat: its military strength (8 per living city plus the combat strength of its living units, js-rounded)
per major seat: its gold, floored
per major seat: its diplomatic favor, floored
per major seat: the civic table indices it holds, ascending
per major seat: its stockpile of each strategic resource, in strategic table order
per major seat: the Great Works of each created kind (writing, art, music) its living cities hold
the scored competition running now (the eras catalog `competitions` index), -1 none
the seat a triggered competition (the Aid Request) is held for, -1 none
per major seat: 1 where it is in the running competition's field
per ordered pair of majors [a][b]: 1 where a is at war with b
[a][b]: the turns the pair's war clock has run
[a][b]: 1 where a's denouncement of b still runs
[a][b]: the turns left on the pair's declared friendship, 0 none
[a][b]: the turns left on the pair's alliance, 0 none
[a][b]: the turns left on a's open-borders grant to b, 0 none
[a][b]: a's delegation or embassy with b, 0 none
[a][b]: the grievances a holds against b (signed)
[a][b]: the least distance between a living city of a and one of b, 999 where either has none; 0 on the diagonal
[a][b]: 1 where a may still declare war on b at all (not at war, not allied or friends, no peace treaty binding)
[a][b]: the turns a's standing deal offer to b still stands, 0 none
[a][b]: that offer's ASK bundle, dealItems slots of [kind, x, y] laid end to end, kind -1 in an empty slot; every value -1 where no offer stands

[a][b]: per promise kind (rules.json eras.promises order: don't spy, don't convert, don't dig, don't settle near), the turns left on b's promise to a (positive) or on b's refusal of a's ask (negative), 0 none
[a][b]: a's living cities following b's religion
world: the engine turn the coming step plays (`state.turn`), the head's `turn`

every living city of every city holder, as [holder seat, centre, followed religion]: the majors in seat order, then the Free Cities (seat 300; TS `cityHolders`), each holder's cities in its city-ARRAY order; the followed religion is the founding seat's index (`City.followedReligion`), -1 none
every living city-state, as [id, centre]: its roster id (fixed for the game) and its CENTRE tile, in the roster's array order (a captured city-state is gone)
the tiles holding a Tribal Village, ascending
static: [T][6] the neighbour tiles of each tile in direction order, -1 off the map
[T][12] the tiles two steps from each tile, ascending, -1 padding
[T][T] the hex distance between two tiles
the city cap the ladder settles to (`seats.maxCities`)
the most living units a seat holds (UNIT_SLOTS)
the specialist pin value that leaves a slot to the automatic rule (SPEC_KEEP)
the unit table rows (rules.json `units`), in table order
the production layout's first unit column (cpu/core/prodLayout.ts)
per district scaffold row: its district id
the Builder's unit table index, -1 none; likewise engineer, missionary, apostle, settler, archaeologist, naturalist
the unit action layout (rules.json `actions.unit`) as name -> column
the PILLAGE column; likewise a_snipe (SNIPE_0), a_snipe3 (SNIPE3_0, -1 none), a_repair (REPAIR)
per improvement table row: its BUILD column, -1 none
the promotion head's width; likewise air_strike_cols, air_rebase_cols, spy_missions (the mission head), spy_travel_cols
the policy card table's size; pol_kind, pol_legacy, pol_dark per card: its slot kind, a legacy card, a Dark Age card
the civic each agreement needs: open_borders_civic, alliance_civic, embassy_civic, joint_war_civic
the gold an embassy costs; delegation_cost a delegation's (whole numbers)
the slots of one deal bundle; deal_kind names each deal item kind's code
the Aid Request's competition index, -1 none
per promise kind (rules.json eras.promises order): the favor an ask costs the asker
